messages:
Lina: FYI customer LensAI opened a high-sev ticket — sudden p95/p99 spike on embed API in prod-east, started ~30m ago. They see 4–6s tails and timeouts. ticket#12345
Omar: any recent deploys to prod-east?
Ashley: no deploys in last 2h from runtime team. saw a burst of new prefixes in the warmup graph at 14:12 UTC.
infra-bot: [ALERT] prod-east kv-evictions rate increased 6x between 14:10-14:25 UTC. p95 latency from 120ms -> 980ms.
Lina: support-bot forwarded their repro: they batch-embed with per-request header X-Client-Session and recently enabled a CDN client fingerprint change. suspect header-driven key explosion?
Omar: can we confirm eviction log + prefix cardinality? Ashley can you paste the warmup/keycard graphs?
Ashley: attaching short log excerpt and counts:
```
eviction_count: 7823
cache_miss_rate: 0.54
unique_prefixes_1m: 89k -> 412k
hot_prefix_top10_rps: skewed
p99_latency_ms: 600 -> 3100
```
Omar: 412k unique prefixes in 1m is huge. that matches header/tenant noise. any header-key normalization in recent change?
Lina: there was a small change in routing that started hashing some headers into the prefix key to improve multi-tenant isolation — intended for A/B of header-based routing. rolled to prod-east ~14:05 UTC.
Omar: that lines up. if we accidentally included session-like header values, the key cardinality explodes and evicts hot prefixes -> thrash. could also observe keyhash collisions if we truncated fingerprint.
Ashley: dumped a few example keys (sanitized):
```
prefix:org:lensai:hdr:accept-language:en-US
prefix:org:lensai:hdr:accept-language:en-US-1234abcdef  <-- session noise
prefix:org:lensai:hdr:x-client-session:abcd1234
prefix:org:lensai:hdr:x-client-session:efgh5678
```
Lina: customer confirms CDN started appending short id to Accept-Language for A/B. so yes — header contains ephemeral ids now.
Omar: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) flip the header-hash flag off for prod-east, 2) enable kv_warmup_circuit to rate-limit warmups, 3) temporarily increase kv cache size for prod-east machines, 4) canonicalize/drop noisy headers at ingress. which can we do fastest?
Ashley: I can flip the flag in the routing config now (no deploy) and enable warmup_circuit feature flag. cache size bump needs infra change (slower).
Lina: please do the flags. Also tell support to ask LensAI to disable the CDN header change while we mitigate.
infra-bot: action_taken: toggled feature routing.include_headers_in_prefix -> false for prod-east (rollout id: r-789).
Lina: toggled — monitoring now.
Ashley: warmup circuit enabled with conservative thresholds; reduced new-prefix admission window to 5k/min.
Omar: watching eviction_count and p99.
Ashley: 10m after flags: eviction_count down 78%, unique_prefixes_1m down to 41k, p99 dropped to ~420ms. still above baseline but improving.
Lina: support updated LensAI: thanks for patience, asked them to revert CDN header patch temporarily. they agreed.
Omar: longer-term fixes: - change prefix key builder to canonicalize and ignore high-entropy headers by default, - improve key hashing (use full SHA256 -> base64 instead of truncated XXHash) to avoid accidental collisions, - tag noisy prefixes + TTL shorter, - add per-tenant sticky prefix bucket to reduce cross-tenant eviction blast.
Ashley: I'll open a runtime PR for canonicalization and shorter TTL for hdr-prefixed keys. Omar can you scope cost if we switch to larger hash (ops + perf), and Lina please coordinate customer comms + postmortem.
Lina: yes — I'll own postmortem and CS follow-up. creating incident doc with timeline, customer impact, and mitigation steps.
support-bot: ticket#12345 updated: temporary workaround applied; awaiting customer revert.
Omar: follow-ups: run a small chaos test that injects header entropy in staging to validate warmup_circuit behavior. also add a Grafana panel for "prefix-cardinality delta" and a runbook step to flip the include_headers flag.
Ashley: repro steps for staging test (copy to runbook):
1) send 1000 embed requests/minute to staging with X-Client-Session randomized per-request
2) measure unique_prefixes_1m and eviction_count
3) validate that warmup_circuit blocks >75% of admission after threshold
4) assert p95/p99 remain < target (500ms/1s)

Curl example:
```
for i in $(seq 1 2000); do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer ${STAGING_KEY}" \
       -H "X-Client-Session: $RANDOM-$RANDOM" \
       -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings &
done
```
Omar: good. make sure we also test with Accept-Language variations since customer CDN used that.
Lina: thanks team — keep updates here. I'll draft the customer-facing timeline once p99 stabilizes.
Ashley: will follow up in ~30m with graphs and PR link.
Omar: +1. once canonicalization PR lands we'll schedule canary in prod-east off-hours.
Lina: incident -> monitoring -> postmortem. closing customer escalation only after 48h stable. :thumbsup:
